topic: What if you acted like GTA 6 in real life for 24 hours?

script.text: Three a.m. A bench in a cold room. No respawn. No save point. Just a very long night.

Eight a.m. Twenty-four hours, exactly. Your mom signs the papers. In the US, a judge has to look at an arrest quickly, usually within forty-eight hours. Then comes the real list. Fines. The taxi fare. And an apology to a man in a bathrobe.

Here's the scoreboard for one day of playing the game for real. A red light ticket. A taxi fare. Charges for running from the police. A lot of new people who know your face. And six hot dogs you'll never be able to look at again.
Rule five lasted eight minutes. Real life keeps every save.
On the steps outside, your phone buzzes. It's Mo. 'Bro. Tomorrow, I'm trying the cheat codes.' Then a second message. 'And this time, you're filming.'

Is any of this real? The facts are. The ten-second sprint. The dog's nose. The thermal camera. The one-phone-call myth. Look them up. And tell me in the comments: which game rule would you break first?

science.claim: In the US, a judge must review a warrantless arrest quickly, generally within 48 hours.
science.working: The Supreme Court held that a probable-cause determination within 48 hours of a warrantless arrest is presumptively prompt.
science.source: County of Riverside v. McLaughlin, 500 U.S. 44 (1991)
